facts.label: official
facts.quote: Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18.
facts.text: Marvel Studios confirmed that 'Avengers: Doomsday' is scheduled to arrive in theaters worldwide on December 18, 2026.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: After a reported production budget of $356M and a comparable marketing budget to boot, the House of Mouse ended up netting $890M — or, if we do really crude math, enough to cover the production budgets of two or three more movies from Marvel Studios.
facts.text: Marvel Studios spent a reported production budget of $356 million to make 'Avengers: Endgame'.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: Another rule of thumb is that theaters keep roughly 50% of the money from ticket sales before the studio gets its cut.
facts.text: Movie theaters retain approximately 50 percent of ticket revenue from ticket sales before a film studio receives its theatrical rental share.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: By the time the studio started seeing money, the box office had already taken about $1 billion of the earnings, giving Disney around $1.789B to pay the bills.
facts.text: Theaters kept approximately $1 billion directly out of the gross box office of Avengers: Endgame before Disney collected its film rentals.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: The shorthand you'll hear from people who actually run these numbers is that a wide theatrical release needs to gross roughly 2.5 times its production budget to get to break-even.
facts.text: Modern box office analysis requires a wide theatrical release to gross roughly 2.5 times its production budget to reach its break-even point.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: China: under the long-standing revenue-sharing import arrangement, foreign rights holders claim roughly 25% of box office — a figure that was raised from the 13–17.5% range under the 2012 US–China film agreement.
facts.text: Foreign studios receive only approximately 25 percent of the ticket sales generated at the theatrical box office in China.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: In fact, the site says Endgame ended up nearly netting Disney a whopping $900 million profit.
facts.text: Avengers: Endgame yielded an estimated net profit of $890 million for Disney after accounting for production, global marketing, and talent participations.

watch.best_change: Open on the payoff, e.g. 'Endgame cost $356M, so it needed nearly $900M just to break even', with that number big on screen in the first second.

script.hook: Avengers: Endgame reportedly cost 356 million dollars. What did it need back?

scenes.label: hook

visual.prompt: Photorealistic wide shot of an enormous film studio set at night, towering lights, cranes and hundreds of crew members working, dramatic sense of scale and expense, cinematic natural haze

scenes.vo: Avengers: Endgame reportedly cost 356 million dollars. What did it need back?

scenes.label: setup

visual.prompt: Photorealistic view of a long queue of excited young Indians outside a multiplex at dusk, holding popcorn, warm evening light, festive buzz.

scenes.vo: Avengers: Doomsday hits theatres this December. Every record will trend. Records are not profit.

scenes.label: belief

visual.prompt: Photorealistic close-up of an Indian hand passing cash across a cinema ticket counter to a cashier, soft indoor light, the moment of payment.

scenes.vo: Most fans think ticket money goes to the studio. It made the film, right?

scenes.label: twist

visual.prompt: Photorealistic shot of a cinema manager in an office counting stacks of rupee notes into two equal piles on a wooden desk, lamp light, serious expression

scenes.vo: Wrong. Theatres keep roughly half of every ticket. In China, foreign studios reportedly get only a quarter.

scenes.label: cost

visual.prompt: Photorealistic view of a busy Mumbai street at night with huge blank movie billboards and posters lining a flyover, crowds and traffic below, no readable text

scenes.vo: And that budget only made the film. Marketing reportedly cost about the same again.

scenes.label: rule

visual.prompt: Photorealistic shot of two film analysts in an Indian office leaning over paper ledgers and a calculator at a table, focused, afternoon window light, no visible numbers.

scenes.vo: Analysts' rule: a big film must earn 2.5 times its budget, just to break even.

scenes.label: payoff

visual.prompt: Photorealistic view from the back of a packed dark cinema hall, rows of silhouetted Indian viewers lit by the glow of the big screen, a sense of a massive hit.

scenes.vo: Endgame crossed that easily, reportedly making Disney a huge profit. For Doomsday, ask one thing: how many times its budget?

scenes.label: send

visual.prompt: Photorealistic shot of two young Indian friends from behind walking out of a multiplex at night, popcorn tubs in hand, chatting, city lights ahead

scenes.vo: Send this to the friend who thinks box office means profit.
